LOVE stamp

The first US Love stamp: an eight-cent issue of 1973 on which Robert Indiana adapted his stacked LOVE image for the United States Postal Service.

Source
Wikipedia: Love (image)
Creator
Robert Indiana, for the United States Postal Service
Made
1973 (issued 26 January 1973)
Style

Moods
Emblematic, bold, popular
Evidence
The National Postal Museum page and the Smithsonian collection record return HTTP 403 to scripts. The only open image found is a 451 × 287 px copy on Wikimedia Commons, too small for observation.

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

In 1973 the United States Postal Service commissioned a stamp design from Indiana and released the eight-cent LOVE stamp before Valentine’s Day. It was unveiled at the Philadelphia Museum of Art, and 425 million were printed over the next two years. Wikipedia).

The image began as a 1964 card that Indiana sent to friends, and in 1965 a red, blue, and green version was chosen for the Museum of Modern Art’s Christmas card. Wikipedia).

The Commons file gives the issue date as 26 January 1973. Commons.

A 1967 screenprint of the same image is Love.

Why it belongs

The stamp shows how far the Pop idiom travelled into everyday print by the early 1970s: a gallery image reduced to postage size still reads because it is one word in four flat colors.

Borrow

Test a Pop headline at icon size: a stacked word in flat color should still read at 40 px.
